subject: English
stem: Identify the part of speech of the word 'clumsily' in: He tripped clumsily on the rug and fell flat on his face.
solution: 'Clumsily' modifies the verb 'tripped', describing the manner of the action, so it is an adverb.

subject: English
stem: Identify the part of speech of the word 'Because' in: Because she was feeling unwell, she decided to avoid the trip.
solution: 'Because' joins the subordinate clause to the main clause, so it functions as a subordinating conjunction.

subject: English
stem: In the sentence 'It is never too late to be what you might have been', the word 'might' is a:
solution: The verb tested is 'be' (in 'to be what you might have been'), a linking/intransitive verb. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Identify the type of verb 'borrowed' in: The student borrowed a pen from her classmate as she had forgotten to get her own pen.
solution: 'Borrowed' takes the direct object 'a pen', so it is a transitive verb.

subject: English
stem: In 'Everyone had gone home by the time she reached the party', identify the form of the verb 'had gone'.
solution: 'Had gone' is the past perfect form, denoting an action completed before another past action (reached). It is a past perfect verb.

subject: English
stem: Remora attaches itself to the shark or whale
optA: by entwining its long body around the bigger fish.
optB: by biting into the fish's body with its teeth.
optC: with an adhesive organ found in its head.
optD: with a hook-like structure in its head.
solution: The passage states the remora uses a sucker on its head to attach itself, that is, an adhesive organ in its head.
context: Among Nature's most intriguing phenomena are the partnerships formed by many different species. The name used for these relationships, Symbiosis, comes from Greek meaning "living together". Not all symbiotic relationships are the same. There are some called commensal relationships, in which one partner gains a benefit while the other gains little or none but is not harmed. One example is the relationship between two types of fish remoras and sharks. The remora, which is long and often striped, attaches itself to a shark (sometimes to another type of fish or a whale), using a sucker on its head. When the shark makes a kill, the hitchhiker briefly detaches itself to feed on the scraps. Another type of symbiotic relationship is parasitism, in which one partner benefits at the expense of others. Ticks and tapeworms are among familiar parasites. The third type of symbiotic relationship, called mutualism, is a true partnership in which both partners benefit. The relationship may be limited as when zebras and wildebeest graze together on the vast African grasslands. Each species can survive on its own, but together their chances of detecting predators are improved because each contributes a specially keen sense. (Zebras have better eyesight; wildebeest, hearing and sense of smell). In a few cases partners are so interdependent that one cannot survive without the other. Most mutualistic relationships probably lie somewhere in between.

subject: English
stem: Commensal relationship is a type of symbiosis in which the relationship is beneficial
optA: to one and harmless to other.
optB: to one and harmful to others.
optD: to both for a very short time.
solution: The passage defines commensal relationships as one partner gaining a benefit while the other gains little or none but is not harmed, that is, beneficial to one and harmless to the other.

subject: English
stem: Threw up my cards
optA: put my whole income at stake
solution: To throw up one's cards means to give up or abandon an effort or plan, that is, gave up my plan.

subject: English
stem: Feather someone's nest.
solution: To feather one's nest means to enrich oneself or provide for one's own needs, usually selfishly.
reviewNote: Idiom traditionally means to enrich ONESELF; printed option (d) 'provide for someone's own needs' is the intended best match.

subject: English
stem: A chip of the old block.
optA: a being of the old generation
optC: a common boy of the locality
optD: someone similar in character to one's father
solution: A chip of (off) the old block refers to a person who closely resembles a parent in character or appearance, that is, someone similar to one's father.

subject: English
stem: An arm-chair critic.
optA: someone who gives advice based on theory not practice
optB: someone who gives advice based on practice not theory
optC: someone who gives advice based on experience
solution: An armchair critic comments or advises on matters without practical experience, basing opinions on theory rather than practice.

subject: English
stem: French leave.
solution: French leave means absence from work or duty without permission, that is, being absent without permission.
reviewNote: Options (a) and (b) are close; (a) 'being absent without permission' is the standard dictionary meaning.

subject: English
stem: He achieved his position through chicanery, not merit.
solution: 'Chicanery' means the use of deception or trickery to achieve a purpose; closest synonym is Trickery.

subject: English
stem: Everyone extolled her for her generosity.
solution: To 'extol' means to praise enthusiastically; closest synonym is Praised.

subject: English
stem: The spread of fake news has a pernicious effect on society.
solution: 'Pernicious' means having a harmful, destructive effect; closest synonym among the options is Deadly.

subject: English
stem: She is extremely fastidious about keeping her room clean.
solution: 'Fastidious' means very attentive to detail and difficult to please; closest synonym is 'hard to please'.

subject: English
stem: Bravery was the most salient feature of his character.
solution: 'Salient' means most prominent or conspicuous; closest synonym is Noticeable.

subject: English
stem: Her winsome smile impressed everyone at the event.
solution: 'Winsome' means attractive or appealing in a charming way; closest synonym is Charming.

subject: English
stem: The moribund company was on the verge of shutting down.
solution: 'Moribund' means at the point of death or in terminal decline; closest synonym is Dying.

subject: English
stem: The recalcitrant student refused to obey school rules.
solution: 'Recalcitrant' means stubbornly resistant to authority; the precise synonym is 'refractory'.

subject: English
stem: After the meeting, he became unusually garrulous and kept talking nonstop.
solution: 'Garrulous' means excessively talkative; closest synonym is Talkative.

subject: English
stem: The customer care centre was inundated with complaints after the outage.
solution: 'Inundated' means overwhelmed or flooded; the closest synonym is Flooded (Filled is weaker and does not capture overwhelming quantity).
reviewNote: (b) Filled and (c) Flooded both plausible; 'Flooded' is the precise synonym of 'inundated'.

subject: English
stem: She decided to relinquish her position to focus on her studies.
solution: 'Relinquish' means to give up or surrender; its antonym is Retain (the other options are synonyms acting as distractors).

subject: English
stem: The country went through a turbulent period marked by protests.
solution: 'Turbulent' means disturbed, stormy and unstable; its antonym is Calm.

subject: English
stem: It is prudent to save money for emergencies rather than spend it all.
solution: 'Prudent' means careful, sensible and cautious; its antonym is Reckless (the other options are synonyms).

subject: English
stem: Trekking through the dense forest was an arduous experience.
solution: 'Arduous' means difficult and demanding; its antonym is Easy (the other options are synonyms).

subject: English
stem: His impeccable manners impressed everyone at the event.
solution: 'Impeccable' means flawless and faultless; its antonym is Defective (the other options are synonyms).

subject: English
stem: The amorphous cloud of smoke spread across the sky.
solution: 'Amorphous' means shapeless and without definite form; its antonym is Structured (the other options are synonyms).

subject: English
stem: He often wastes time discussing trivial matters at work.
solution: 'Trivial' means of little importance; its antonym is Important (the other options are synonyms).

subject: English
stem: She gave a candid reply about her mistakes.
solution: 'Candid' means frank, open and honest; its antonym is Secretive (the other options are synonyms).

subject: English
stem: The leader delivered a profound speech that moved the audience.
solution: 'Profound' means deep and meaningful; its antonym is Shallow (the other options are synonyms).

subject: English
stem: The criminal remained elusive despite several attempts to trace him.
solution: 'Elusive' means hard to find, catch or pin down; its antonym is Obvious (the other options are synonyms).

subject: English
stem: Your success in the IAS examinations depends not only on (a)/ what papers you have selected (b)/ but on how you have written them. (c)/ No error. (d)
solution: The correlative is used in parallel here ('not only on ... but on ...'); 'also' is optional, so the sentence is correct. No error, option D.
reviewNote: Correlative pair error: 'not only...but (also)'. Error in (c). | aligned to official LWS key.

subject: English
stem: Heavy rain (a)/ prevented us (b)/ to go to the cinema. (c)/ No error. (d)
solution: 'Prevent' is followed by 'from + verb-ing', not the infinitive; 'to go' should be 'from going'. The error is in part (c).

subject: English
stem: He asked (a)/ supposing if he fails (b)/ what he would do. (c)/ No error. (d)
solution: In reported speech the verb should backshift to 'supposing if he failed' (not 'fails') to agree with the past 'asked'. The error is in part (b).

subject: English
stem: We had a lot of difficulty (a)/ to find (b)/ the house. (c)/ No error. (d)
solution: 'Difficulty' is followed by 'in + verb-ing'; 'to find' should be 'in finding'. The error is in part (b).

subject: English
stem: Patience as well as perseverance (a)/ are necessary (b)/ for success. (c)/ No error. (d)
solution: With 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first (singular) subject 'Patience'; 'are' should be 'is'. The error is in part (b).

subject: English
stem: The passer-by told us (a)/ where was the marriage hall (b)/ and even led us to it. (c)/ No error. (d)
solution: An indirect question keeps statement word order: 'where the marriage hall was', not 'where was the marriage hall'. The error is in part (b).

subject: English
stem: The increase in consumption is directly (a)/ proportional to the increase (b)/ in income. (c)/ No error. (d)
solution: The sentence is grammatically correct: 'directly proportional to' is the correct idiom. There is no error, so (d).

subject: English
stem: In Singapore (a)/ my brother-in-law with his wife (b)/ were present at the function. (c)/ No error. (d)
solution: The subject is singular 'my brother-in-law' (with his wife is parenthetical), so the verb should be 'was', not 'were'. The error is in part (c).

subject: English
stem: Scarcely had (a)/ I arrived when (b)/ the train left. (c)/ No error. (d)
solution: 'Scarcely had I arrived when the train left' is grammatically correct: 'Scarcely/Hardly' takes the correlative 'when', and the past-perfect inversion 'Scarcely had I arrived' is standard. There is no error, so (d).
reviewNote: LOW CONFIDENCE: Scarcely...when is correct usage, so (d) No error is the defensible key; some banks mark (b). Verify against the official LWS key.

subject: English
stem: He is one of those writers (a)/ who has won (b)/ acclaim worldwide. (c)/ No error. (d)
solution: In 'one of those writers who ...', the relative 'who' refers to the plural 'writers', so the verb should be 'have won', not 'has won'. The error is in part (b).

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Statement I: Volcanic eruption is accompanied by earthquakes. Statement II: Volcanoes erupt water vapour and dust particles into the atmosphere. Choose the correct option regarding the above statements.
optA: Both the statements are individually true and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I.
optB: Both the statements are individually true but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I.
optC: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
optD: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
solution: Both statements are individually true: rising magma and ground rupture do trigger earthquakes during eruptions, and volcanoes do eject water vapour, gases and dust into the atmosphere. But Statement II (what is ejected) does not explain Statement I (why eruptions are accompanied by earthquakes), so II is not the correct explanation of I. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Consider the following statements relating to the Richter Scale: 1. It was devised in 1935 by Charles F. Richter. 2. It measures the magnitude of an earthquake by describing the energy released. 3. The Richter Scale has no fixed upper limit. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: All three are correct: the Richter scale was devised in 1935 by Charles F. Richter, it measures earthquake magnitude based on the energy released, and it is open-ended with no fixed upper limit. Matches option D: 1, 2 and 3.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: While travelling to a hilly region, you notice a massive boulder that was loosened by heavy rains and moved downhill. This movement has occurred due to which of the following processes? 1. Mass wasting 2. Erosion 3. Weathering Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: A boulder loosened and moving downhill under gravity is mass wasting; erosion needs transport by an agent and weathering is in-situ breakdown, so only 1 applies. Matches option A.
reviewNote: dup of df8e78a5 | aligned to official LWS key.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which of the following statements with respect to landslides are correct? 1. They occur only on gentle slopes during rainfall. 2. They generally occur in clay-rich soils. 3. Earthquakes can trigger landslides. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Statement 1 is wrong (landslides occur on steep, not gentle, slopes). Statements 2 (clay-rich soils are prone) and 3 (earthquakes trigger landslides) are correct. Matches option C: 2 and 3 only.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: The point of origin of an earthquake wave inside the Earth is known as:
solution: The point of origin of an earthquake within the Earth is the Focus (or hypocentre). The epicentre is the point on the surface directly above the focus. Matches option B: Focus.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. Hypocentre is the point on the surface of the Earth nearest to the focus. 2. The velocity of earthquake waves is higher in denser materials. 3. P-waves move faster and are the first to arrive at the Earth's surface. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Statement 1 is incorrect: the hypocentre IS the focus (inside the Earth); the epicentre is the surface point. Statement 2 is correct (seismic velocity increases in denser media) and Statement 3 is correct (P-waves are fastest and arrive first). Matches option B: 2 and 3.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which of the following statements with reference to L-waves (Long waves) generated by an earthquake is/are correct? 1. They travel along the Earth's surface following its curvature. 2. They move at nearly constant speed. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: L-waves travel along the Earth surface following its curvature (1) and move at a nearly constant speed (2), so both statements are correct. Matches option C.
reviewNote: dup of ff48e2a6 | aligned to official LWS key.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which of the following statements with reference to shadow zones during an earthquake is/are correct? 1. The zone between 105° and 145° from the epicentre is identified as the shadow zone for both P-waves and S-waves. 2. The shadow zone of P-waves is larger than that of S-waves. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: The 105 to 145 degree belt is the shadow zone where neither P nor S waves arrive directly, so statement 1 is correct; statement 2 is wrong, so only 1 holds. Matches option A.
reviewNote: dup of 62199b79 | aligned to official LWS key.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which of the following statements regarding earthquakes is/are correct? 1. The point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus is called the epicentre. 2. Earthquakes generate Primary (P) and Secondary (S) waves that radiate outward from the focus. 3. Deep-focus earthquakes are likely to cause more damage than shallow-focus earthquakes. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — shallow-focus earthquakes cause more surface damage than deep-focus ones because the released energy is closer to the surface. Matches option B: 1 and 2 only.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: A large body of magmatic material that cools at great depth within the Earth's crust and develops in the form of large domes is known as:
solution: A batholith is a very large mass of intrusive igneous rock that cools deep in the crust and is later exposed by erosion as large dome-shaped structures. Matches option A: Batholith.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Which one of the following is a crater lake in India?
solution: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra was formed by a meteorite impact and is a classic crater lake. Sambhar is a salt lake, Chilika is a lagoon, and Vembanad is a backwater. Matches option A: Lonar Lake.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is the deepest and largest intrusive igneous body?
solution: A batholith is the largest and deepest intrusive igneous body, forming the base of mountain ranges. Laccolith, lopolith and phacolith are smaller, shallower intrusions. Matches option B: Batholith.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is formed when volcanic ash is carried by running water and deposited as a sedimentary layer?
solution: When volcanic ash is transported by running water and deposited, it consolidates into a rock called tuff. Basalt is solidified lava, lapilli is loose pyroclastic fragments, and slate is a metamorphic rock. Matches option D: Tuff.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Vapours of sulphur escaping from a volcano often form a crust on surrounding rocks. The process involved is an example of:
solution: Sulphur vapour changing directly into solid sulphur (a crust) without passing through the liquid state is the gas-to-solid phase change called deposition (desublimation). Condensation is gas to liquid and evaporation is liquid to gas. Matches option C: Deposition.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Which of the following statements about the Ring of Fire is/are correct? 1. It is a zone of convergent plate boundaries. 2. It is an active seismic and volcanic zone. 3. It is associated with deep ocean trenches. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: The Pacific Ring of Fire is a horseshoe-shaped belt of convergent (subduction) plate boundaries (1), is the most active seismic and volcanic zone on Earth (2), and is bordered by deep ocean trenches such as the Mariana and Peru-Chile trenches (3). All three are correct. Matches option D: 1, 2 and 3.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Which one of the following is a major tectonic plate?
solution: The Pacific Plate is one of the seven major tectonic plates. The Cocos, Arabian and Philippine plates are minor plates. Matches option A: Pacific Plate.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. Oceanic trenches are significant in the study of plate movements. 2. Oceanic trenches are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Both statements are correct: oceanic trenches mark subduction zones that are central to the study of plate movements (1), and these subduction zones are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes (2). Matches option C: Both 1 and 2.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Which one among the following volcanic island chains is NOT associated with a mid-oceanic ridge?
solution: The Hawaiian Islands are formed by a mantle hotspot (plume), not by a mid-oceanic ridge. The Azores, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha lie on or near the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. Matches option C: Hawaiian Islands.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Which one of the following is a major plate?
solution: The Pacific Plate is one of the seven major tectonic plates; the Cocos, Arabian and Philippine plates are minor plates. Matches option A: Pacific Plate.
reviewNote: internal dup of Q66 (also bank aca17958)

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Which one of the following is not a minor plate?
solution: Cocos, Nazca and Caroline are minor plates; the Antarctic Plate is one of the seven major tectonic plates. So it is the one that is NOT a minor plate. Matches option D: Antarctic Plate.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. Oceanic trenches are very significant in the study of plate movements. 2. Oceanic trenches are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Both statements are correct: oceanic trenches mark subduction zones important for plate tectonics, and these zones are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes. Matches option C: Both 1 and 2.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Which of the following statements about the Ring of Fire is/are correct? 1. It is a zone of convergent plate boundaries. 2. It is an active seismic and volcanic zone. 3. It is associated with deep oceanic trenches. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: The Ring of Fire is a zone of convergent (subduction) plate boundaries (1), the most active seismic and volcanic zone (2), and is bordered by deep oceanic trenches (3). All three are correct. Matches option D: 1, 2 and 3.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Advantages of tectonic activity in Iceland include: 1. Source of natural geothermal energy 2. Creation of new land 3. Attraction of tourists Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Iceland's location on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge gives it geothermal energy (1), new land created by lava flows (2), and tourist attractions such as geysers and volcanoes (3). All three are advantages. Matches option D: 1, 2 and 3.

subject: Geography
stem: Mariana Trench is located in the ocean floor of:
solution: The Mariana Trench, the deepest oceanic trench, lies in the Western Pacific Ocean near the Mariana Islands. Matches option B: Western Pacific Ocean.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Which of the following statements regarding Earth's internal structure is/are correct? 1. The oceanic crust is heavier than the continental crust. 2. Most of the Earth's internal heat is contained within the mantle. 3. Large convective cells in the crust circulate heat and drive plate-tectonic processes. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Statement 1 is correct (oceanic crust is basaltic and denser/heavier). Statement 2 is correct (most internal heat is held in the mantle). Statement 3 is incorrect — the large convective cells that drive plate tectonics operate in the mantle, not the crust. Matches option B: 1 and 2 only.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: In which one of the following folds is the axial plane found to be virtually horizontal?
solution: In a recumbent fold the strata are overturned so far that the axial plane becomes nearly horizontal. In isoclinal and anticlinal folds the axial plane is steep or vertical. Matches option C: Recumbent.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is not an example of a Fold Mountain?
solution: Mt. Fuji is a composite (volcanic) mountain, not a fold mountain. The Alps, Andes and Rockies are all fold mountains formed by plate collision. Matches option A: Mt. Fuji.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following gases is found in highest quantity in the exosphere?
solution: The exosphere, the outermost atmospheric layer, is dominated by the lightest gases; hydrogen is present in the highest quantity, with helium next. Matches option A: Hydrogen.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following gases is placed second in respect of abundance in the Earth's atmosphere?
solution: Earth's atmosphere is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen. Nitrogen is most abundant and oxygen is second in abundance. Matches option A: Oxygen.

subject: Geography
stem: Dinitrogen (N2) and dioxygen (O2) are the main constituents of air but they do not react with each other to form oxides of nitrogen because:
optA: The reaction requires initiation by a catalyst
optC: The reaction is endothermic and requires very high temperature
optD: The stoichiometry of N2 and O2 in air is not ideal for the reaction to take place
solution: The combination of nitrogen and oxygen to form nitric oxide is strongly endothermic, so under ordinary conditions the reaction does not proceed. It occurs only at the very high temperatures found in lightning discharges or internal-combustion engines. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of atmospheric layers as we move from the Earth's surface upwards?
solution: From the Earth's surface upward the layers are Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Thermosphere (then Exosphere). Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: The normal lapse rate of temperature of Earth's atmosphere drops to 0°C at the:
solution: Temperature falls with height at the normal lapse rate through the troposphere and stops falling at the top of the troposphere — the tropopause. Matches option B: Upper boundary of the tropopause.

subject: Geography
stem: In which one of the following layers of the atmosphere do all weather phenomena occur?
solution: All weather phenomena — clouds, rain and storms — occur in the troposphere, which holds the water vapour and dust and is the site of convection. Matches option B: Troposphere.

subject: Geography
stem: Consider the following statements with reference to the structure of the Earth's atmosphere: 1. Thickness of the troposphere is greatest at the equator. 2. The air temperature of the tropopause is highest above the poles. 3. The temperature in the troposphere decreases at the rate of 1°F for every 165 m of height. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: The troposphere is thickest over the equator, so statement 1 is correct; statements 2 and 3 are not accepted, so only 1 holds. Matches option A.
reviewNote: dup of 77c5e8fb | aligned to official LWS key.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements about temperature is correct?
optA: Temperature decreases with height in the stratosphere
optB: Temperature is constant at different heights in the stratosphere
optC: Temperature increases with height in the troposphere at an average rate of 6.5°C per kilometre
optD: Temperature decreases with height in the troposphere at an average rate of 6.4°C per kilometre
solution: In the troposphere temperature decreases with height at the normal lapse rate (about 6.4–6.5°C per km). In the stratosphere temperature increases with height. So only option D is correct. Matches option D.
reviewNote: dup of efcf5492 (bank twin states 6.5; this paper's correct option D states 6.4 — the only true statement among the four)

subject: Geography
stem: When heat rays are reflected from the Earth, gases like carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide do not allow them to escape back into space, causing our planet to heat up. These gases are known as:
solution: Gases such as carbon dioxide, nitrous oxide, methane and water vapour absorb the long-wave (heat) radiation emitted by the Earth and prevent it escaping to space, warming the planet — the greenhouse effect. They are called greenhouse gases. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not a greenhouse gas?
solution: Water vapour, methane and ozone are greenhouse gases. Carbon monoxide is a pollutant but not a direct greenhouse gas. Matches option D: Carbon monoxide.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following greenhouse gases is present in the largest concentration in the atmosphere?
solution: Among the listed greenhouse gases, carbon dioxide is present in the largest concentration in the atmosphere; methane, nitrous oxide and CFCs occur in much smaller amounts. Matches option C: Carbon dioxide.

subject: Geography
stem: The Earth's atmosphere is mainly heated by which one of the following?
solution: The atmosphere is largely transparent to incoming short-wave solar radiation; it is heated chiefly by the long-wave terrestrial radiation emitted by the Earth's surface after it absorbs that solar energy. Matches option C: Longwave terrestrial radiation.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not a main greenhouse gas?
solution: Water vapour, carbon dioxide and methane are major greenhouse gases. Oxygen is not a greenhouse gas. Matches option B: Oxygen.

subject: Geography
stem: What happens when sunlight travels through the Earth's atmosphere?
optA: The blue colour is scattered more compared to the red colour
optB: The red colour is scattered more compared to the blue colour
optC: Both the blue and the red colours are scattered equally
optD: The blue colour is not scattered but the red colour is scattered the most
solution: By Rayleigh scattering, the shorter-wavelength blue light is scattered much more than the longer-wavelength red light, which is why the daytime sky appears blue. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem: One of the main causes of air pollution in cities is emissions from vehicles like cars and trucks. Cars emit various pollutants which are harmful to human health when inhaled, such as:
solution: Among the listed vehicle emissions, nitrogen oxides are taken as the intended harmful pollutant. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Flawed as a single-answer item — all four are emitted by vehicles; treated as the list for the linked Q93. Closest single answer: Carbon monoxide. | aligned to official LWS key.

subject: Geography
stem: Of the vehicle pollutants — 1. Nitrogen oxides (NOx), 2. Carbon monoxide (CO), 3. Carbon dioxide (CO2), 4. Benzene — which are not tolerated by human beings even at very low levels?
solution: Nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide and benzene are toxic and harmful to humans even at very low concentrations. Carbon dioxide is a normal constituent of air and is tolerated at low levels (it is harmful only in high concentrations). So the not-tolerated pollutants are 1, 2 and 4. Matches option D: 1, 2 and 4 only.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is a cause of acid rain?
solution: Acid rain is caused mainly by sulphur dioxide (and nitrogen oxides), which dissolve in atmospheric moisture to form sulphuric and nitric acids. Matches option C: Sulphur dioxide.

subject: Geography
stem: The poisonous nature of carbon monoxide (CO) is due to its:
optB: Ability to form a complex with haemoglobin
optC: Ability to reduce some metal oxides
optD: Property of having one sigma bond
solution: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin much more strongly than oxygen, forming a stable carboxyhaemoglobin complex. This blocks the blood from carrying oxygen, which makes CO poisonous. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is the usual unit of measurement for air pressure used in India?
solution: Atmospheric (air) pressure is measured in millibars (or hectopascals) in meteorology, and India uses the millibar as its standard unit for air pressure. Matches option B: Millibar.

subject: Geography
stem: Mariana Trench is located in the ocean floor of:
solution: The Mariana Trench, the deepest oceanic trench, lies in the Western Pacific Ocean near the Mariana Islands. Matches option B: Western Pacific Ocean.
reviewNote: internal dup of Q74 (also bank c18ce16c)

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. Oceanic trenches are very significant in the study of plate movements. 2. Oceanic trenches are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Both statements are correct: oceanic trenches mark subduction zones central to plate-tectonic study, and these zones are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes. Matches option C: Both 1 and 2.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Which of the following statements about the Ring of Fire is/are correct? 1. It is a zone of convergent plate boundaries. 2. It is an active seismic and volcanic zone. 3. It is associated with deep oceanic trenches. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: The Ring of Fire is a zone of convergent (subduction) plate boundaries (1), the most active seismic and volcanic zone (2), and is bordered by deep oceanic trenches (3). All three are correct. Matches option D: 1, 2 and 3.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem: Which of the following statements with regard to the Western Coastal Plain of India are correct? 1. It is a narrow belt. 2. It is an example of a submerged coastal plain. 3. It provides natural conditions for the development of ports. 4. It has well-developed deltas. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: The Western Coastal Plain is a narrow belt (1), a submerged coastal plain (2), and its submerged character provides natural harbours and ports such as Mumbai (3). It lacks well-developed deltas — rivers flowing into the Arabian Sea form estuaries, not deltas; deltas characterise the eastern coast. So statement 4 is wrong. Matches option A: 1, 2 and 3 only.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. The Earth's crust is brittle in nature. 2. The mean thickness of the oceanic crust is 15 km, whereas that of the continental crust is around 30 km. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Both statements are taken as correct: the crust is brittle (1) and the quoted mean thicknesses (oceanic about 15 km, continental about 30 km) are accepted (2). Matches option C.
reviewNote: dup of 7b130de4 | aligned to official LWS key.

subject: Physics
stem: If a lens is cut into two pieces perpendicular to the principal axis and only one part is used, the intensity of the image
solution: Cutting a lens perpendicular to the principal axis does not change its aperture, so the same amount of light is gathered and the image intensity remains the same. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: The reason of seeing the Sun a little before the sunrise is
solution: Atmospheric refraction bends sunlight as it passes through layers of air of increasing density, making the Sun visible slightly before it actually rises above the horizon. Matches option B.
reviewNote: dup of fd66d570 (same physics: atmospheric refraction makes Sun visible before sunrise)

subject: Physics
stem: Which mirror is to be used to obtain a parallel beam of light from a small lamp?
solution: A concave mirror, with the lamp placed at its focus, reflects the rays as a parallel beam. This is the same principle used in vehicle headlights and torches. Matches option C.
reviewNote: dup of 51ff20ad (concave mirror in headlights sends parallel rays — same concept of source at focus of concave mirror)

subject: Physics
stem: Two thin lenses whose powers are +2D and -4D respectively combine, then the power of combination is
solution: For lenses in contact, powers add: \(P = P_1 + P_2 = (+2) + (-4) = -2\) D. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: Near and far points of human eye are
solution: For a normal human eye the least distance of distinct vision (near point) is about 25 cm and the far point is at infinity. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: The frequency of a light ray is \(6 \times 10^{14}\) Hz. Its frequency when it propagates in a medium of refractive index 1.5, will be
solution: Frequency of light is set by the source and does not change on entering a medium; only the wavelength and speed change. So it remains \(6 \times 10^{14}\) Hz. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: Refractive index of glass with respect to medium is \(\frac{4}{3}\). If the difference between velocities of light in medium and glass is \(6.25 \times 10^{7}\) ms\(^{-1}\), then velocity of light in medium is
solution: Refractive index of glass w.r.t. medium \(= \frac{v_{medium}}{v_{glass}} = \frac{4}{3}\). Let \(v_{glass} = x\), so \(v_{medium} = \frac{4}{3}x\). Difference \(\frac{4}{3}x - x = \frac{1}{3}x = 6.25 \times 10^{7}\), giving \(x = 1.875 \times 10^{8}\) and \(v_{medium} = \frac{4}{3}(1.875 \times 10^{8}) = 2.5 \times 10^{8}\) ms\(^{-1}\). Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: The human eye can focus objects at different distances by adjusting the focal length of the eye lens. This is due to
solution: The ciliary muscles change the curvature (and hence the focal length) of the eye lens to focus objects at different distances; this ability is called accommodation. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: Which cells respond to colour of light?
solution: Cone-shaped cells in the retina are sensitive to colour and function in bright light, while rod cells respond to dim light and brightness only. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: How many electrons in 1 s constitute a current of 1 A?
solution: A current of 1 A means 1 coulomb of charge flows per second. Number of electrons \(= \frac{1}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}} = 6.25 \times 10^{18}\). Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: 1 Coulomb is equal to \(-\)
solution: Charge \(Q = I \times t\), so 1 coulomb = 1 ampere \(\times\) 1 second. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: When a body is negatively charged by friction, it means-
optA: the body has acquired excess of electrons
optB: the body has acquired excess of protons
optC: the body has lost some electrons
optD: the body has lost some neutrons
solution: Charging by friction transfers electrons. A body that becomes negatively charged has gained (acquired excess of) electrons. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: A wire of resistance R is cut into n equal parts. These parts are then connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance of combination will be \(-\)
solution: Each of the n equal parts has resistance \(\frac{R}{n}\). Connecting n such equal resistances in parallel gives \(R_{eq} = \frac{R/n}{n} = \frac{R}{n^2}\). Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: A piece of wire of resistance 4 \(\Omega\) is bent through \(180^\circ\) at its mid-point and the two halves are twisted together, then resistance is -
solution: Each half of the 4 \(\Omega\) wire has resistance 2 \(\Omega\). Twisting the two halves together connects them in parallel: \(R_{eq} = \frac{2 \times 2}{2 + 2} = 1\,\Omega\). Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: In the given circuit, the effective resistance between points A and C will be - (Square ABCD with A top-left, D top-right, C bottom-right, B bottom-left; side A-D = R, side D-C = R, side A-B = R, side B-C = R, and a diagonal A-C = 2R.)
solution: Between A and C there are three independent paths: the diagonal A-C = 2R; the route A-D-C = R + R = 2R; and the route A-B-C = R + R = 2R. B and D are not otherwise connected, so the three 2R paths are in parallel: \(\frac{1}{R_{eq}} = \frac{1}{2R} + \frac{1}{2R} + \frac{1}{2R} = \frac{3}{2R}\), giving \(R_{eq} = \frac{2R}{3}\). Matches option C.
reviewNote: Circuit figure read from rendered PDF page 10: square ABCD with side R on each of A-D, D-C, A-B, B-C and a diagonal A-C of 2R. Three parallel 2R paths between A and C.

subject: Physics
stem: How much electrical energy in kilowatt hour is consumed in operating ten, 50-watt bulbs for 10 hours per day in a month of 30 days?
solution: Total power = \(10 \times 50 = 500\) W = 0.5 kW. Energy = power \(\times\) time = \(0.5 \times 10 \times 30 = 150\) kWh. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: The resistance of a conductor is reduced to half its initial value. In doing so the heating effects in the conductor will become
solution: At constant applied voltage, heat \(H = \frac{V^2}{R}t\). If R is halved, H doubles. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Standard reading: voltage held constant (domestic supply), so H = V^2/R t and halving R doubles heating; option D.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: The magnetic field intensity produced due to a current carrying coil is maximum at-
optC: any point lying on the axis of the coil
optD: points lying between centre of the coil and its circumference
solution: For a circular current-carrying coil the magnetic field is strongest at the centre of the coil and decreases as one moves along the axis away from it. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: Which of the following determine the direction of magnetic field due to a current carrying conductor?
solution: Maxwell's right-hand cork-screw rule gives the direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor. (Fleming's left-hand rule gives force direction; Faraday's/Lenz's laws govern induced emf.) Matches option D.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: A length of wire carries steady current. It is bent first to form a circular plane coil of one turn. The same length is now bent to give a double loop of smaller radius. The magnetic field produced at the centre by the same current will be-
optA: a quarter of its first value
solution: Field at centre \(B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2r}\). For one turn of radius \(r_1\), \(L = 2\pi r_1\). For a double loop (N = 2) the same length gives \(L = 2(2\pi r_2)\), so \(r_2 = \frac{r_1}{2}\). Then \(B_2 = \frac{\mu_0 (2) I}{2 (r_1/2)} = 4 \cdot \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 r_1} = 4 B_1\). Matches option C.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: Which of the following statement is not correct about two parallel conductors carrying equal currents in the same direction?
optA: Each of the conductors will experience a force
optB: The two conductors will repel each other
optC: There are concentric lines of force around each conductor
optD: Each of the conductors will move if not prevented from doing so
solution: Two parallel conductors carrying currents in the same direction ATTRACT each other, not repel. Hence the statement that they repel is not correct. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: A.C. used in our domestic consumption has a frequency-
solution: Domestic AC supply in India has a frequency of 50 Hz. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: Current is induced in a coil by electromagnetic induction when
optA: Only the coil moves in a magnetic field
optB: Only the magnet is moved into a coil
optC: Coil and the magnet move with respect to each other
solution: An emf is induced whenever there is relative motion between the coil and the magnet (changing flux). This covers all cases, so the most complete statement is that the coil and magnet move with respect to each other. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: AC is preferred because \(-\)
solution: AC can be stepped up to high voltage with transformers, reducing transmission losses, making it economical for transmission over long distances. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: Choose the correct option. The magnetic field inside a long straight solenoid carrying current
optB: decreases as we move towards its end.
optC: increases as we move towards its end.
optD: is the same at all points.
solution: Inside a long straight current-carrying solenoid the magnetic field is uniform (the same at all points). Matches option D.
reviewNote: dup of 3d36ba53 (identical stem and option set; bank answer 'is uniform' = printed option D 'is the same at all points')

subject: Physics
stem: At the time of short-circuit, the current in the circuit
solution: In a short circuit the resistance drops to nearly zero, so by Ohm's law (I = V/R) the current increases heavily. Matches option C.
reviewNote: dup of 062aca8e (same concept and answer: short-circuit current increases substantially/heavily)

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: Magnetic field is produced by the flow of electric current in a straight wire. This phenomenon was discovered by
solution: Hans Christian Oersted discovered that an electric current produces a magnetic field around the conductor. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: A magnetic field exerts no force on
optC: an electric charge moving perpendicular to its direction
solution: The magnetic force on a charge is \(F = qvB\sin\theta\); for a stationary charge \(v = 0\), so the force is zero. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: Which of the following instruments works by electromagnetic induction?
solution: A dynamo (AC/DC generator) converts mechanical energy to electrical energy using electromagnetic induction (Faraday's law). Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: The use of fuses in electric power-lines is
optA: just to show an indication when there is an overload
optB: as a switch to use in an emergency
optD: to open the line permanently when there is an overload
solution: A fuse is a safety device with a low-melting-point wire that melts and breaks (opens) the circuit when the current exceeds a safe limit (overload/short circuit). Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: When the main switch of the house circuit is put off, it disconnects the
solution: The main switch is a double-pole switch that disconnects both the live and the neutral wires of the house circuit. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: Potential difference between a live wire and the neutral wire is
solution: In the Indian domestic supply the potential difference between the live and neutral wires is 220 V. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: A magnetic field
optA: always exerts a force on a charged particle
optB: never exerts a force on a charged particle
optC: exerts a force, if the charged particle is moving across the magnetic field lines
optD: exerts a force, if the charged particle is moving along the magnetic field lines
solution: The magnetic force \(F = qvB\sin\theta\) is non-zero only when the charge moves with a component across (perpendicular to) the field lines; it is zero for motion along the field. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following types of medicine is used for treating indigestion caused by over-eating?
solution: Indigestion is caused by excess acid in the stomach. An antacid (a mild base such as magnesium hydroxide or sodium bicarbonate) neutralises the excess acid and relieves the discomfort. Antibiotics treat infection, analgesics relieve pain, antiseptics kill germs on surfaces. Matches option C: antacid.
reviewNote: dup of 6f8e5c6b-6e48-41c8-8e7a-2e19852f627e (same concept; bank answer Antacid, here printed as option C)

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: A solution reacts with marble chips to produce a gas which turns lime water milky. The solution contains:
solution: Marble chips are calcium carbonate. Only an acid reacts with \(\text{CaCO}_3\) to liberate \(\text{CO}_2\), which turns lime water milky: \(\text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \to \text{CaSO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2\). Of the four salts, only \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) is an acid; the others are neutral salts that do not react with marble. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: One of the following is not an organic acid. This is:
solution: Organic acids contain carbon bonded to carbon or hydrogen in carboxyl groups (ethanoic, formic and citric acids are all carboxylic/organic acids). Carbonic acid \(\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\) is classed as an inorganic (mineral) acid even though it contains carbon, because it is formed from \(\text{CO}_2\) and water and lacks a C-H/carboxylic organic framework. Matches option D: carbonic acid.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The indicators which turn red in acid solution are:
solution: In acid, blue litmus turns red and methyl orange turns red (pink). Phenolphthalein is colourless in acid (pink only in base), and turmeric stays yellow in acid (turns red-brown only in base). So the two indicators that turn red in acid are litmus and methyl orange. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: A solution reacts with zinc granules to give a gas which burns with a pop sound. The solution contains:
solution: A gas that burns with a pop sound is hydrogen. Zinc reacts with an acid to liberate \(\text{H}_2\): \(\text{Zn} + 2\text{HCl} \to \text{ZnCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\). Of the options only \(\text{HCl}\) is an acid; \(\text{Mg(OH)}_2\) and \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\) are basic/salt and \(\text{NaCl}\) is a neutral salt, none of which give \(\text{H}_2\) with zinc. Matches option D.

subject: Chemistry
stem: A solution turns phenolphthalein indicator pink. The most likely pH of this solution will be:
solution: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic and neutral solutions and turns pink only in basic solution (pH above about 8.2). Of the options, only pH 9 is basic. Matches option C: 9.

subject: Chemistry
stem: One of the following salts will give an alkaline solution on dissolving in water. This is:
solution: A salt of a strong base and a weak acid hydrolyses to give an alkaline solution. \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\) (strong base NaOH, weak acid \(\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\)) gives an alkaline solution. \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4\) and \(\text{NaCl}\) are salts of strong acid and strong base (neutral); \((\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4\) is a salt of strong acid and weak base (acidic). Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The salt which will give a neutral solution on dissolving in water will be:
solution: A salt of a strong acid and a strong base does not hydrolyse and gives a neutral solution. \(\text{KCl}\) (from strong acid HCl and strong base KOH) is neutral. \(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}\) and \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\) are alkaline (weak acid + strong base); \(\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}\) is acidic (strong acid + weak base). Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: An element X reacts with hydrogen, when heated, to form a covalent hydride \(\text{H}_2\text{X}\). If \(\text{H}_2\text{X}\) has a smell of rotten eggs, the element X is likely to be:
solution: The hydride with a rotten-egg smell and formula \(\text{H}_2\text{X}\) is hydrogen sulphide, \(\text{H}_2\text{S}\). Sulphur has valency 2 (Group 16), consistent with \(\text{H}_2\text{X}\). Carbon gives \(\text{CH}_4\), chlorine gives HCl, phosphorus gives \(\text{PH}_3\). Matches option B: sulphur.

subject: Chemistry
stem: An element X forms two oxides XO and \(\text{XO}_2\). The oxide XO is neutral but \(\text{XO}_2\) is acidic in nature. The element X is most likely to be:
solution: Carbon forms two oxides matching the description: carbon monoxide (CO) is a neutral oxide, and carbon dioxide \((\text{CO}_2)\) is an acidic oxide. Sulphur's common oxides \((\text{SO}_2, \text{SO}_3)\) are both acidic; calcium forms only the basic oxide CaO; hydrogen forms only neutral water. Matches option B: carbon.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Zinc oxide is a metal oxide. Which of the following term best describes the nature of zinc oxide:
solution: Zinc oxide \((\text{ZnO})\) reacts with both acids and bases, so it is an amphoteric oxide: with acid it forms a salt and water, and with strong base it forms a zincate. Matches option C: an amphoteric oxide.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Reactivity Series and Reactions with Water
stem: An element E reacts with water to form a solution which turns phenolphthalein solution pink. The element E is most likely to be:
solution: A pink phenolphthalein colour indicates a basic (alkaline) solution. Calcium reacts with water to form calcium hydroxide, a base: \(\text{Ca} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{H}_2\). Sulphur and carbon are non-metals forming acidic/neutral oxides; silver does not react with water. Matches option B: Ca.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Atomic Number, Mass Number and Subatomic Particles
stem: The atomic number of an element Y is 17. The number of electrons in its ion \(Y^{-}\) will be:
solution: A neutral atom of atomic number 17 (chlorine) has 17 electrons. The \(Y^{-}\) ion has gained one electron, giving 17 + 1 = 18 electrons. Matches option B: 18.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The atomic numbers of four elements A, B, C and D are 6, 8, 10 and 12 respectively. The two elements which can react to form ionic bonds (or ionic compound) are:
solution: A (Z=6) is carbon, B (Z=8) is oxygen, C (Z=10) is neon (inert), D (Z=12) is magnesium. An ionic bond forms between a metal and a non-metal. Magnesium (D, metal) and oxygen (B, non-metal) transfer electrons to form ionic MgO. Carbon forms covalent bonds, neon is unreactive. Matches option D: B and D.
reviewNote: B (oxygen) and D (magnesium) form ionic MgO; option D selected.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The number of protons in the nucleus of one atom of an element Y is 5. The symbol of ion formed by an atom of this element will be:
solution: An element with 5 protons is boron, electronic configuration 2, 3. It has 3 valence electrons which it loses to attain a stable octet, forming a tripositive cation \(Y^{3+}\). Matches option D: \(Y^{3+}\).

subject: Chemistry
stem: A covalent molecule having a double bond between its atoms is:
solution: The oxygen molecule \(\text{O}_2\) has a double bond (O=O) between its two atoms. Hydrogen \((\text{H}_2)\) has a single bond; water \((\text{H}_2\text{O})\) and ammonia \((\text{NH}_3)\) contain only single covalent bonds. Matches option B: Oxygen.
